conversation.contentPreview:
Create a complete single self-contained file `chip8_openai-gpt-5.6-terra_01.html` (HTML + CSS + JavaScript inline;
no external libraries, CDNs, assets or backend). Build a working CHIP-8 emulator.

Implement the interpreter properly: 4 KB of memory with the font set loaded at 0x050 and programs at 0x200,
sixteen 8-bit registers V0 to VF, the 16-bit index register, the program counter, a call stack, and the
delay and sound timers counting down at 60 Hz. Decode and execute the complete instruction set of 35
instructions, including the arithmetic and logic group with the carry and borrow flags in VF, the shift
instructions, jumps and calls, the random instruction, BCD conversion, register save and load, and the key
tests.

The display is 64 by 32 pixels drawn on a canvas scaled to a readable size, with sprites drawn by XOR and
the collision flag set in VF. The 16-key keypad is mapped to a 4 by 4 block of keyboard keys shown in the
interface; key press and release must both reach the emulator.

Include a small demo ROM as a byte array inside the file: a real program, assembled by you, that draws a
sprite and moves or reacts to a key, so that the emulator can be tried without any download. Also allow
loading a ROM from a local file.

Add run, pause, single step and reset controls, an adjustable instructions-per-frame speed, and a debugger
panel showing the registers, the index register, the program counter, the stack and the decoded current
instruction. Every visible control must work. Deliver the one file `chip8_openai-gpt-5.6-terra_01.html`.

{"path":"chip8_openai-gpt-5.6-terra_01.html","edit_description":"Create this new single, fully self-contained HTML file implementing a polished working CHIP-8 emulator (all CSS and JavaScript inline; no external assets/libraries/network). Build an accessible dark themed page headed “CHIP-8 Studio”, with a large 64x32 canvas display scaled with pixelated rendering, an emulator status indicator, controls Run, Pause, Step, Reset, Load demo, a labelled local ROM file chooser, speed range slider (instructions/frame) with live value, and a clearly labelled keypad legend in a 4 by 4 visual grid. Implement all controls and keyboard mapping (1 2 3 4 / Q W E R / A S D F / Z X C V mapped to CHIP-8 hexadecimal 1 2 3 C / 4 5 6 D / 7 8 9 E / A 0 B F); keyboard down/up must update CHIP-8 keys and visual keys. Prevent default only for mapped keys while focus is not typing/file input. Include a debugger panel showing 16 registers V0-VF, I, PC, delay timer, sound timer, stack, decoded next/current opcode, and ROM label, updated during execution.

Implement a correct CHIP-8 interpreter in inline JS: memory Uint8Array(4096), V Uint8Array(16), I, PC initialized at 0x200, stack (array with max 16), delayTimer and soundTimer, display Uint8Array(64*32), keys Uint8Array(16), font bytes loaded at 0x050, programs loaded from 0x200. Render white/cyan pixels on canvas at 10x resolution with a readable canvas width 640 height 320 and pixelated image rendering. Include a 60 Hz timer accumulator via requestAnimationFrame and decrement delay/sound timers accurately at 60 Hz. Per animation frame, execute adjustable number of instructions if running and update render/debugger. Properly protect invalid PC/memory/stack errors and show status.

Decode the canonical full 35 instruction behaviors, including: 00E0, 00EE, 1nnn, 2nnn, 3xkk, 4xkk, 5xy0, 6xkk, 7xkk, 8xy0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7,E, 9xy0, Annn, Bnnn (classic V0 offset), Cxkk, Dxyn (XOR sprite collision VF and wrap 64x32), Ex9E, ExA1, Fx07, Fx0A (wait for a fresh keypress without advancing PC), Fx15, Fx18, Fx1E, Fx29, Fx33, Fx55, Fx65. Use SCHIP-independent classic CHIP-8 semantics. In 8xy6 and 8xyE use Vx as source (set VF to outgoing bit then shift Vx); Fx55/Fx65 leave I unchanged. Decode errors should pause and surface clear status. decodeInstruction(opcode) must produce useful assembly-like strings for debugger.

Embed a genuine demo ROM as a byte array assembled in JS, not an external download. It should reset/clear then use V0,V1 as X/Y, update coordinate in response to the mapped left/right/up/down keys (A/F/W/S for CHIP-8 keys 7/E/5/8 respectively), clamp/wrap positions, and draw an 8x5 sprite using DxyN each loop with a small delay. Put its bytes at program start and sprite bytes after executable code. It must load and run with Load demo and Reset. Initial state should load demo but start paused. Local file load should use FileReader ArrayBuffer, check max 3584 bytes, load/reset ROM, identify label, and pause. Reset should reload the active ROM. Step works when paused (one instruction, render/debug refresh). On Run set running, Pause clear running. Add succinct in-page help explaining the keyboard map and demo movement.

Use no external resources. Ensure all visible buttons/inputs have event handlers, UI has high contrast, responsive layout, and JavaScript is syntactically valid."}
